### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `objectstack-blank`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/objectstack.config.ts`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/objectstack.config.ts`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `requiredPermissions (literal, 40 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **190** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d80cbd4503c37e2995941bc41d6e49ca2e09f441` — the merge of head `fce0fd912ccea5e400f10ad2c329804b54821e03` into base `e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d80cbd4503c37e2995941bc41d6e49ca2e09f441 && git checkout d80cbd4503c37e2995941bc41d6e49ca2e09f441
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472 fce0fd912ccea5e400f10ad2c329804b54821e03 && git checkout -B drift-repro e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472 && git merge --no-ff fce0fd912ccea5e400f10ad2c329804b54821e03

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e4bfa339ab09cbdfcf897aa079134b7cf5810472` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e6bae722d0073a4a4a9b096cb79b9aac0d3b677a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-namespace-rename.ts, packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/declared-capability-context.ts
Security-touching: yes

PR #35261 for card #35157. Read: the card body and every comment (record 6999763503 rules item 1, option A), the PR body, its 47-file list and the net diff against the merge-base with `main`, and the 73 check-runs on this head (every one success or skipped, the eleven required contexts success). The tree is judged, not the PR body: the body still reads "awaits the maintainer's ruling" and says nothing of the head commit's anchor change.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Registry flag** (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts`): `capability` goes from `allowRuntimeCreate: false` to `true`; `supportsOverlay` and `allowEnvironmentOverlay` stay `false`. Right, and it is what record 6999763503 rules. Everything keyed on the flag follows with no second list: `RUNTIME_UNCREATABLE_TYPES` in `stack.zod.ts` stops naming `capability`, so `defineStack` no longer refuses `installModes: ['unmanaged']` for an app that declares one, and the type catalogue serves the type as creatable. Right.
- **Save door accept set**: a `capability` save moves from 403 `NOT_CREATABLE` to accepted. The body is judged by the strict `CapabilityDeclarationSchema` (422 `INVALID_METADATA`); a platform capability's name and a name another holder holds answer 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. Read on the head: the refusal runs on a draft save and a publish save (`protocol-save.ts`), on promote (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts`) and on the restore doors (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts`), by singular type, and the platform-name refusal comes before any read. Right.
- **Package door and cold boot** (`security-catalog-namespace.ts`): `capability` joins `ENVIRONMENT_HELD_SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES`, so the package-held name listing the save door reads now carries capability names, an install over an environment-held capability name is refused, and a cold boot refuses a configured package's capability name the environment also holds. Right as a rule; the remedy the boot prescribes does not reach a capability row (S3).
- **Rename engine** (`package-namespace-rename.ts`, one engine for `duplicatePackage` and `importUnmanagedPackage`): a declared capability whose name carries the source namespace prefix is renamed, and the two keys are rewritten in list form and in the per-operation map form; an undeclared name is untouched; a copy name the package already declares is refused at its own name. Right as far as it goes, incomplete at three edges (S1).
- **Anchor context** (`declared-capability-context.ts`): only registry declarations stamped `_packageId` reach `declaredCapabilities`. Manifest and nested-plugin declarations are stamped with their owner at registration, and the curated platform declarations register under the platform's own package id, so no shipped app loses its exemption; the platform floor in `describeHighPrivilegeBits` is untouched. The narrowing is real for a package-less row only (S2).
- **Remainder**, named and not reviewed here (the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`): tests and fixtures, the changesets' prose, `content/docs/**`, the `create-objectstack` blank template, `ui/**` (the draft panel and the locale packs), and the comment-only hunks in `objectql` (`registry.ts`, `registry-namespaces-and-claims.ts`, `index.ts`), `plugin-security` `access-upgrade-report.ts` and `runtime` `catalog-activation.ts`.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35157-unmanaged-copy-capabilities.md` declares `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/objectql`, `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, with `Metadata-protocol: added`. Right: a save the door refused is now accepted, and a kind other than `none` puts the level at minor or above. All four packages are in the fixed group, so the `patch` publishes at the group's level.
- The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line holds, on the PR body and on the changeset alike. The accept set grows: one type moves from 403 to accepted, and `unmanaged` is admitted for an app that declares a capability. Two things tighten and neither takes away anything a supported door on `main` could produce, because no door on `main` wrote a capability row: the cold boot now refuses a stored capability row under a package-declared name (the changeset says so), and the anchor counts package-bound declarations only.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds: no skill teaches capability as code-only, the scaffold's plugin list or the unmanaged install, and the docs pages that did are in this diff.
- The other two changesets belong to the remainder. One observation for the lane seat, ungraded: `.changeset/35157-scaffold-no-connector-plugins.md` declares `minor` under `Metadata-protocol: none`, where the level rule gives `patch`. The fixed group publishes at minor either way and Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Item 1's fork** (Claim 6995599332 and the PR body): answered by record 6999763503, option A, maintainer verbatim 「同意」. The PR body's "awaits the maintainer's ruling" is superseded by that record; nothing here rests on the body.
- **ADR-0126 amendment, owed**: at this head ADR-0126 still lists `capability` among the code-only types (the tier table, and §9's "not chartered" line). Record 6999763503 puts the amendment note in a separate governed PR; the thread names no such PR and no card. Escalated to the adopting seat: file it so the ADR and the registry do not disagree on `main` once this lands (Prime Directive 13).
- **Escalated to the maintainer, with S2**: record 6999763503 says this PR "closes a gap the risk review found: an environment-saved capability is not excused at the `everyone` anchor". The head closes it for a package-less row only. A save addressed to a writable base (`?package=BASE`, the package-first address of ADR-0070 and the address the unmanaged import itself writes to) registers the declaration with `_packageId`, and it is excused. Under option A a filter on the row cannot close this, because a hand-saved package capability and a copied one are the same row. The bound that holds on this head is: a platform capability's name and a package-declared name can never be declared at runtime; every other name is excused, and its `scope` is decided, once a `manage_metadata` holder declares it inside a package. The maintainer should confirm that bound or order a stricter one.
- **Not ruled, untouched by this diff**: keeping a template's own namespace by default, and reserving official prefixes (record 6999763503 says no card is filed). cloud#4856 (the double prefix on unmanaged copies) is cloud-side and not taken; this diff adds no exposure to it.
- **Card items 2 and 3**: the scaffold change and the tests are remainder, not reviewed here.
- **Stated narrowing**: a cold boot now refuses when a stored capability row sits under a name a configured package declares. The changeset states it.
- **SQL push-down**: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The capability holder read at the save door goes through the same cached per-type active-row read the permission-set check already uses.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. S1 to S3 below each earn a delta review; four nits follow.

What held against an attempt to break it:

- **Shadowing the platform or a package.** A runtime save under any name in `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_NAMES` is refused before any read. A name a package holds, by composite slot or install claim, is refused on draft, publish, promote and restore. A package install over an environment-held name is refused, and so is a cold boot over one. `catalog.resolve` answers the bare slot first, and no door on this head lets an environment row into the bare slot under a held name.
- **A door around the refusal.** Every protocol method that writes a capability body (`saveMetaItem`, `publishMetaItem`, `publishPackageDrafts`, the restore and revert writers, `duplicatePackage`, `importUnmanagedPackage`) reaches `permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal`; there is no rename door. The unmanaged import is all-or-nothing and deletes its base when one item is refused.
- **Forged provenance.** A body-supplied `_packageId` is stripped and re-stated from the row's `package_id` column, so the body cannot claim a holder or a package it is not stored under.
- **Two gates merged inside one copy.** A copy name the package already declares is refused, and only declared, prefixed names are renamed, so a platform token or another package's token in the copy's lists stays exactly as the source wrote it.

**S1 (should-fix) — `package-namespace-rename.ts`: the rename follows a capability under two keys only, so a renamed copy can name a capability its own declaration does not carry.**

- (a) `CAPABILITY_REFERENCE_KEYS` holds `systemPermissions` and `requiredPermissions`, and its docblock says ADR-0066 D1 "names no third edge". The published spec names one: `page.zod.ts` teaches `visibleWhen` to gate a component with `current_user.hasCapability('NAME')` "with the name the gated action's `requiredPermissions` declares", and `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` teaches the same pairing. The engine rewrites the action's requirement to the copy's name and leaves the predicate naming the source's. In the copy, a holder of the copy's capability has the component hidden, and a holder of the source's capability sees it and is refused by the action. No grant widens, since the requirement is what refuses, but the copy no longer behaves as the app it copies.
- (b) `rewrite()` runs the capability pass first and then hands its output to `deepRewrite`, whose object-name pass rewrites inside every string, the two keys' values included; the declaration's own `name` is set by `copyName` alone. A capability whose name embeds a renamed object's name between separators splits in two: with namespace `crm` copied as `shop` and object `crm_invoice`, the capability `crm.crm_invoice.void` is declared in the copy as `shop.crm_invoice.void`, while the copy's sets grant and its actions require `shop.shop_invoice.void`. The gate still matches by string, but the token the copy grants is declared nowhere, so it loses its label and its `scope`, reads as undeclared at the `everyone` anchor and as "declared nowhere" at the organization boundary. The comment above the call says the object pass "must not be what decides a capability's copy name"; on this path it does.
- (c) The docblock says an unprefixed capability's second holder "is refused at the save door, loudly, never shared". That is true of the declaration row. `duplicatePackage` copies item by item, so the refused declaration is one `failed[]` entry while the duplicate's sets and actions land naming the source's capability: the shared gate the paragraph above sets out to prevent. A capability refused by the in-package copy-name check ends the same way at that door. Only the all-or-nothing import door keeps the sentence true.
- Direction: rewrite a renamed capability inside `hasCapability` arguments, or refuse the copy of an item whose predicate names a renamed capability the engine did not rewrite; keep the object-name pass out of the two keys' values, so a declaration and its references get one name; and at `duplicatePackage`, refuse or report the items that keep a capability whose declaration was not copied, with the docblock corrected to what the door does.

**S2 (should-fix) — `declared-capability-context.ts`: the package filter does not deliver what its comment, the changeset and the docs page say it does.**

- The filter keeps a registry declaration when it carries a non-empty `_packageId`. That stamp is the row's package binding (`withRowBinding`, from the `package_id` column), and the author chooses the binding by addressing the save to any writable base. So the comment's "an environment save registers it in this same collection with no `_packageId`" is true of a package-less save only, and the harm it names, "counting it would let a metadata author excuse any name from the anchor gate by saving a declaration of it", is still open one query parameter away. The one-holder reading, which this diff extends to capabilities, takes that row the other way: "every bare-slot item is the environment's whatever `_packageId` it wears" (`registry-namespaces-and-claims.ts`).
- The same overclaim is published: the changeset's "A capability saved through the metadata door excuses nothing, so a metadata author cannot clear a token for `everyone` by declaring it", and `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx` ("A capability saved this way is not an app's own token at the `everyone` anchor").
- What bounds it on this head is the two name floors, and they hold: a platform capability's name is refused and stays high-privilege by name, and a package-declared name is refused. What is left open is every other name, including a token a shipped package grants or requires without declaring it. For such a token a `manage_metadata` holder can now declare it inside a writable base, which excuses it at the `everyone` anchor and, through the declaration's `scope`, decides condition (c) of the organization boundary (`organizationBoundaryFailure` reads the resolved declaration with no provenance test). On `main` both belts refused that token because nothing could declare it at runtime.
- The second source is unfiltered: when the registry lists no capability at all, the `metadataService.list('capability')` answer is returned whole, package-less declarations included.
- Direction: state the bound that holds in the comment, the changeset and the docs page, or enforce the stricter one if the maintainer orders it (③); and give the metadata-service branch the same provenance test, or drop it for this reader. Graded below a refusal of the head because the enforced behaviour is the only one consistent with option A (an unmanaged copy's capabilities must count), both floors hold, and the actor already holds a platform-scope capability.

**S3 (should-fix) — `security-catalog-namespace.ts`: the cold boot now refuses over a capability name and prescribes a remedy that cannot see a capability row.**

- Adding `capability` to `ENVIRONMENT_HELD_SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES` makes the boot refuse when a configured package declares a capability name the environment holds. The refusal text (`coldBootConflictMessage`) tells the operator that `os migrate security-catalog-overlays` "lists every such row with no server running, and with --apply deletes them". That command's `STORED_TYPE_SPELLINGS` (`packages/cli/src/utils/security-catalog-overlays.ts`, outside this diff) reads the position and permission spellings only, so it lists nothing for a capability.
- The state is reachable through this PR's own feature: an unmanaged copy that keeps its namespace stores the app's capability names as environment rows; configuring the same app later as a managed package refuses the next cold boot over them. The server is down, so the metadata door cannot delete the rows, and the one prescribed tool does not list them.
- Direction: teach the command the `capability` and `capabilities` spellings in the same change that makes the boot refuse over them, or have the message stop prescribing it for a capability.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit): the registry entry's `description` still reads "A permission a package defines; you grant it through permission sets". An environment can define one now.
- N2 (nit): the module doc of `security-catalog-namespace.ts`, "The cold boot", still says the boot asks for "every package-held position and permission-set name". Stale statements of the same kind sit in the remainder or outside the diff, read and not reviewed: `registry-namespaces-and-claims.ts` ("the two types the environment can author"), the `protocol.ts` docblock of `permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal`, `metadata-create-seeds.ts` ("for `capability`'s reason") and the sharing-rule migration entry's text ("the `capability` pair").
- N3 (nit): the capability pass has no counterpart to the object pass's entry-collision refusal. A list holding a renamed name and an undeclared name equal to its copy name ends with one name twice. Contrived, since the source would have to name a token in the target's namespace.
- N4 (nit, follow-up card suggested): the cold boot reading skips built-in names. A stored capability under a name a later release adds to `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_NAMES` would not be refused at boot and would answer `catalog.resolve` from the bare slot, `scope` included, ahead of the platform's declaration. No state on this head reaches it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `706dbee6a4b722979aac85aec23989bb26f4ba6d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-namespace-rename.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/declared-capability-context.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/security-catalog-overlays.ts
Security-touching: yes

Delta review of PR #35261 for card #35157 (record 7000301544: PASS on the previous head, S1 to S3 open, nits N1 to N4). Read: the two commits between that head and this one (11 files; the second commit adds three import lines to one test file), ruling record 7000639892 on the card, the card and PR threads as they stand, and the check-runs on this head and on the intermediate commit. The hits file and the two save-door files are byte-identical to what record 7000301544 judged, and its judgment of them carries. The tree is judged, not the PR body, which is unchanged and still reads "awaits the maintainer's ruling".

The check-runs on this head were still running when this record was rendered (29 created: 5 success, 6 skipped, 18 running, none red; no lint, type-check or test lane had reported), so the derived gate families are not yet answered on it. On the intermediate commit the push of this head cancelled the test and type-check lanes; of the lanes that finished there, one gate was red, the Test-source alias gate, over the CLI integration test that commit edited. It prescribed three module-top imports, and the second commit adds exactly those three. This record judges the design of the delta and rests on no local run; the required contexts still have to turn green on the head that lands.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Rename engine** (`package-namespace-rename.ts`): a capability name is now rewritten in three places, the two keys and a quoted `hasCapability('NAME')` argument (`HAS_CAPABILITY_CALL`), and in those places the object-name pass no longer runs. Right for a name the package declares: declaration, grant, requirement and predicate get one name. Wider than that for a name it does not declare (S4).
- **Duplicate door** (`protocol-package-commits.ts`): `duplicatePackage` passes the new optional input `sourceStaysInstalled: true`. With it the plan refuses a declared capability the copy cannot rename, and every item that names one under the two keys or in a quoted predicate, each at its own name in `failed[]`. Right: the source is a stored base that stays beside its duplicate. The unmanaged import does not pass it; read again on this head, that door raises every plan refusal before the base exists and deletes the base when a save is refused, so it stays all-or-nothing.
- **Anchor context** (`declared-capability-context.ts`): the metadata-service branch is filtered by the same `_packageId` test as the registry branch; the comment states the bound that holds. Right, and it is what record 7000639892 rules.
- **Remedy command** (`packages/cli/src/utils/security-catalog-overlays.ts`): `STORED_TYPE_SPELLINGS` gains `capability` and `capabilities`, so the listing meets the same package-held reading the cold boot refuses on. A capability row is deleted through `SysMetadataRepository.delete` with `intent: 'runtime-only'`, which the repository's gate admits for a type that is runtime-creatable; the protocol's delete door is not used because it reads the managed seal for a type with no overlay channel. Right; the cold boot's prescription is now true for a capability row.
- **Module doc** (`security-catalog-namespace.ts`): "The cold boot" names the capability. Right.
- **Remainder**, named and not reviewed here (the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`): the tests in `package-namespace-rename.test.ts`, `builtin-capabilities.test.ts` and the CLI integration test, the changeset prose, `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`, and the text-only hunks of `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/security-catalog-overlays.ts`.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset gains `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. Right: the remedy command reads one more row class and no command surface changes; `@objectstack/cli` is in the fixed group and publishes at the group's level.
- `minor` on spec, metadata-protocol and objectql with `Metadata-protocol: added`, and the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, are unchanged and still hold. The new duplicate refusals take away nothing `main` could produce: they arise only for a stored base that declares a capability, and no door on `main` stored one.
- One change this delta makes to what a copy contains for an input `main` accepts is not stated in the changeset (S4).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The escalation with S2 is answered**: record 7000639892, maintainer option 「接受现有边界」. The bound stands as it holds on the tree, no stricter refusal is built, and the record corrects the sentence of record 6999763503 that this review questioned.
- **ADR-0126 amendment, still owed**: neither thread names a PR or a card for it at this read. Still escalated to the adopting seat (Prime Directive 13).
- **Gates not yet answered on this head, to the adopting seat**: see the check-run paragraph above. The one red gate of the intermediate commit is answered by the test-only commit on top of it, and no lane had reported on this head at this read.
- **Stated deviation in the remedy command**: a capability row leaves a history tombstone and no audit row, because the audited door refuses it. The module header says so and each outcome names the door it took. Flagged for the adopting seat: the header cites the two deletion doors to the ruling on #22371, which predates capability rows, and this delta sends a canonical spelling through the door the module used for legacy plurals only.
- **Not ruled, untouched**: keeping a template's own namespace by default, and reserved official prefixes. cloud#4856 is not taken.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. S1, S2 and S3 are closed on this head. S4 is new in this delta and earns a delta review. N1, N3 and N4 stand; N2 is fixed; N5 and N6 are new.

**S1: closed.**

- (a) A quoted `hasCapability` argument follows the capability rename, in single or double quotes, any number of calls per string; any other argument is left as written, and the docblock says so. The docblock no longer claims there is no third edge.
- (b) The values under the two keys and the quoted argument skip the object-name pass, and the declaration's `name` comes from the same map, so `crm.crm_invoice.void` is `shop.crm_invoice.void` in the declaration, the grant, the requirement and the predicate.
- (c) At the duplicate door a declared capability the copy cannot rename is refused with every item that names it, so no copied item grants, requires or tests for a capability the source still declares. The docblock now describes each door as it behaves.
- The split of a string around each call leaves the object-name pass unchanged for every string that holds no such call.

**S2: closed.**

- The comment, the changeset bullet and the docs page now state the bound the head enforces: a declaration bound to a package is excused, one saved with no package is not, a platform capability's name and a package-declared name cannot be declared at runtime, and any other name can be declared once by a `manage_metadata` holder inside a writable package, which decides its `scope`. Record 7000639892 accepts that bound.
- The metadata-service branch applies the same provenance test.

**S3: closed.**

- The command the cold boot prescribes lists a capability row over a package-held name and deletes it, addressed by spelling, name, `package_id` and checksum. The repository gate admits the delete on the `runtime-only` intent for this type, and the row is read back by id after the delete.

**S4 (should-fix) — `package-namespace-rename.ts`: the object-name exemption also covers names the package does not declare, so a copy now keeps a token that on `main` followed its object, and shares the source's gate.**

- The fix for S1 (b) takes every value under the two keys, and every quoted `hasCapability` argument, out of the object-name pass. For a name the package declares that is right, because the capability rename decides it. For a name the package does not declare nothing decides it, and it is copied as written.
- On `main`, and on the previous head, the object-name pass read those strings like any other. A token that contains a renamed object's name as a whole word followed the object: with object `crm_invoice` copied as `shop_invoice`, an undeclared `crm_invoice.void` became `shop_invoice.void` in the grant, the requirement and the predicate alike, so the copy had a gate of its own. On this head the copy keeps `crm_invoice.void` in all three places. A holder of the copy's set passes the source's action, and a holder of the source's set passes the copy's. Two unmanaged copies of one app under two namespaces meet the same way.
- The tokens this reaches are the ones stored bases hold today: before this PR no door stored a capability declaration, so a base authored in the environment grants and requires undeclared tokens only. The duplicate door's new refusal does not see them, since `sharedCapabilities` is built from declared names, and nothing reports them; the copy lands clean.
- The changeset and the docs page describe the new rule ("The object-name rename never reads those places"; "copied as written") and do not say that an undeclared token used to follow its object.
- Direction: let the capability rename decide the names the package declares and leave every other entry to the object-name pass, as on `main`; or keep the new rule, state the change in the changeset and the docs page, and have the duplicate door report an undeclared token it leaves shared with the source. The direction S1 (b) carried on record 7000301544 ("keep the object-name pass out of the two keys' values") was wider than the defect it answered; the defect was the declared name.
